newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom making full enquiry in Ericsson affair.
newsitem.headline: Telekom making full enquiry in Ericsson affair.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd said on Thursday it was carrying out full investigations into alleged irregularities in awarding a contract to Swedish telecoms firm LM Ericsson.

"Immediately on being alerted by Deputy Prime Minister (Anwar Ibrahim), Telekom Malaysia has taken action to make a thorough enquiry into these allegations," Telekom's chief executive Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali said in a statement issued by the company.

"This is a serious allegation and Telekom Malaysia will do everything in its power to get to the truth. As far as Telekom Malaysia is concerned, we have always adhered to our established procedures on receiving, considering and awarding of tenders," said Mohamed Said.

He said the company cannot give a specific timeframe when the investigations will yield results "since we do not at this stage have sufficient facts on the matter, but it will be a top priority for Telekom Malaysia to resolve this issue as soon as we can".
On Wednesday, Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he had received a report that there may have been "discrepancies" in a contract awarded by Telekom to Ericsson.
Anwar said he has not been able to verify the authenticity of the report and has asked Telekom to look into the matter.
Ericsson said on Wednesday it had no comment concerning this particular case but suspected it was connected to earlier rumours of criminal and unethical actions.

"We haven't yet been able to confirm what has actually been said but we suspect this has been a connection to the rumours spread by a business contact in the Middle East," Ericsson's head of information Lars Stalberg told Reuters in Stockholm.
"These reports have been spread all over the world, including Malaysia," he said.
Ericsson has said in a statement on December 20 last year that the company had been the subject of serious allegations concerning deliveries to the Middle East. It had denied the allegations.
In September, the Swedish firm announced it had signed a 960 million crown contract with Telekom for delivery of AXE telecommunications systems over two years.
Negative sentiment over the investigation dragged Telekom stock 40 cents down to close at 20.60 ringgit ($8.30) on Thursday.
